statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 14% and remains below the watch threshold, while Stress is elevated at 56% because long-end Treasury yields, oil and gold are all pressing at once.
recommendation: The mapped policy state stays EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 13:30Z to 15:00Z covering the US cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI release. The elevated Stress reading reflects cross-asset conflict rather than observed one-way Nasdaq-100 structure; retracements are still available in the current price path.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures bounce about 0.7% after a five-day slump, but a 4.71% 10-year yield keeps the recovery conditional.
body: NQ futures trade near 29,510, roughly +0.7%, holding the upper half of a 29,274-29,538 overnight range after five consecutive losing sessions for the Nasdaq-100. The bounce is not confirmed across assets: the 10-year yield sits near 4.71% and the 30-year near 5.25% after this week's bond rout, Brent is near $94 on expectations of new US measures against Iran, and gold is up around 1.7% on the day, a combination that reads as hedging rather than a clean risk-on turn. VIX near 15 and uniformly positive megacap and semiconductor performance in the latest session argue against panic. No persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern is observed in the current price path, so Tail stays low at 14% while Stress is held elevated at 56%. The near-term checkpoint is the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMI pair, whose prices components can transmit directly into the long end and from there into a yield-sensitive index; the 13:30Z cash open falls in the same window. Scores step to watch level for 13:00Z-14:00Z and decay afterwards on the assumption that price discovery is orderly. US index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the second half of the forecast horizon carries a closed-market floor with a slow confidence decay.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: five hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z) and the remaining nineteen clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available slots Tail stayed tightly contained between 12% and 13% with a green mapped state throughout, Stress decayed steadily from 59% to 53% as the overnight session traded without one-way structure, and Confidence improved from 83% to 87% as more of the session's evidence became verifiable.
outlookSummary: The forecast steps up to watch level for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours, which contain the US cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI pair, then decays back toward the current baseline through the New York afternoon on the assumption that price discovery stays orderly and the 10-year holds near 4.71%. A modest rise is carried into the 19:00Z power hour for weekly-close positioning. From 21:00Z US index futures are halted for the weekend, so the remaining fourteen slots carry a closed-market floor: Tail falls to 6-8% because no tradable price path exists, Stress sits in the low-to-moderate band reflecting accumulating weekend headline exposure through the Iran sanctions and oil channel, and Confidence decays slowly from 75% to 65% purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation.
